title: Metal Organic Framework-Derived Metal Phosphates as Electrode Materials for Supercapacitors

nodes.label: Supercapacitor electrodes need high specific capacitance with rate capability; MOFs offer surface area but conduct and cycle poorly
Substituting the BTC ligands of a Ni-MOF with phosphate should give a metal phosphate that keeps the rod architecture and adds redox-active, better-conducting framework
Ni-BTC MOF of 1D zigzag chains as the precursor and shape template
Hydrothermal ligand substitution with sodium phosphate at 150 C for 75 h, rather than calcining the MOF away
Pristine Ni-MOF against the derived phosphate, over 1-100 mV/s, 1-20 A/g and 10 000 cycles

attrs.levels: MOF / derived phosphate; 1-100 mV/s; 1-20 A/g; 10 000 cycles at 6 A/g

nodes.label: Treat the Ni-MOF hydrothermally with sodium phosphate so phosphate ions take the place of the BTC ligands
Carboxylate coordination of BTC is replaced by P-O and O-P-O bonding in the derived solid
The derived solid is largely amorphous with a weak crystalline texture matched to a nickel phosphate card
The derived solid inherits the microrod form of the MOF but the rods swell and their surfaces become loose and rough
Surface porosity opens up and the specific surface area rises from 2.51 to 142.24 m2/g
Sheet resistance of the electrode film falls from 1049.42 to 714.13 ohm/sq after substitution
Charge storage is Faradaic, through a quasi-reversible Ni(II)/Ni(III) redox couple, not double-layer
Specific capacitance reaches ~1630 F/g at 1 A/g, four times the pristine MOF, and still ~1045 F/g at 20 A/g
Loose porous rods shorten the ion path and expose more redox-active Ni sites while the phosphate framework carries charge better, so capacitance and rate capability rise

attrs.mechanism_class: ion transport and redox site accessibility

nodes.label: The electrode keeps about 54% of its capacitance after 10 000 cycles at 6 A/g at near-unity coulombic efficiency
Ligand substitution turns a Ni-MOF into a porous metal phosphate that works as a high-capacitance supercapacitor electrode
The Nyquist panel gives the derived electrode the larger arc, so the claimed drop in charge-transfer resistance is not shown
The rods are called hollow, but no cross-section or transmission view is shown that could resolve an interior void
The derived phosphate is thermally more stable than the MOF, losing 25% of its mass to 600 C against the MOF's ~88%
The sharp BTC bands of the MOF at 1624, 1565, 1436 and 1338 cm-1 are absent from the derived spectrum

nodes.label: Ni-BTC forms 1D zigzag chains of tetraaqua-nickel(II) units cross-linked by hydrogen bonding into a 3D network
Infrared bands at 1120-910 cm-1 are P-O stretching and at 600-530 cm-1 O-P-O bending
JCPDS card 04-010-2575 gives the reflections of Ni2(PO3)4
A loosely bound porous electrode shortens the ion diffusion length, takes up more ions and accommodates volume change during redox
Phosphate groups stabilise the framework and help electron transfer during redox

notes: Single-branch conversion paper: one synthesis step produces four structure claims (bonding, phase, rod shape, porosity) that meet again at the mechanism e14 and the capacitance e13. Numbers are read from the panels: band positions from the labels on F2a, step sizes from F2b, discharge times ~720 s against ~180 s at 1 A/g from F5c/F5d, ~1630 to ~1045 F/g with the printed 64% from F5e, and ~1090 to ~580 F/g over 10 000 cycles from F5g. Two audits. e17 with OBS f11: the Nyquist panel F5f gives the derived electrode the LARGER, unclosed arc while the MOF arc closes near 10 ohm, the opposite of the text's 'smaller semicircle'; only the high-frequency intercept in the inset favours the derived (~1.0 vs ~1.4 ohm), which is series, not charge-transfer, resistance. e18: the rods are called hollow throughout but only surface views are shown. Further figure-text conflicts kept in image_note rather than as nodes: the FTIR panel labels the third BTC band 1338 cm-1 where the text says 1373 cm-1; weak features remain in the derived trace where the text says the BTC bands disappeared; F3b's indexed positions are card sticks over two broad amorphous humps, so 'good agreement' is weak; F5c and F5d show discharge branches only and F5d carries one sample although its caption names both; the F5g cycling curve steps down near 1800 cycles. Packet figure ids are offset by one from the paper's numbering because Scheme 1 takes packet F1, so packet F2-F5 are paper Figures 1-4 and the panel ids follow the packet. OCR defects: the F4a label was read as (B) although the panel is (a), and F4b's bar was read as '2m' where the burnt-in banner reads 1 um. Lost: the EDS of Figure S2, the energy-density/Ragone claim, the redox equations and the two-electrode device data.

panel_checks.note: F5f opened. The derived electrode's arc is the larger one and is still rising at Z' = 14 Ohm, while the MOF arc peaks near -Z'' 4.7 Ohm and is closing by 10 Ohm; the inset gives intercepts of ~1.0 and ~1.4 Ohm. The node reads the panel exactly, and calling it a contradiction of the text rather than a gap in it is right.

F5e prints 64% and 19% on the panel and the two series run ~1630 -> ~1045 F/g and ~400 -> ~85 F/g over 1-20 A/g, as the node states. The packet's definition string credits this panel to the derived electrode alone although it carries both.

F4a is smooth faceted microrods, F4b thicker rods blanketed in granular particles and loose debris, both with a 1 um bar burnt into the banner at x15,000 and x16,000. Neither is a cross-section, so the e18 audit about the unresolvable interior void is right. Packet OCR defects on this figure: F4a's label is read as (B) when the panel is (a), and F4b's 1 um bar is read as '2m'.

review.audit_summary: Three audits, all genuine and all correctly distinguished. e17 with OBS f11 is a figure-contradicts-text finding, verified on the crop: the text claims a narrowed semicircle and lower charge-transfer resistance for the derived electrode and the panel shows the opposite, so e17 qualifies both the conductivity claim e11 and the mechanism e14, while f11 still records the one thing the panel does support, the lower high-frequency intercept. e18 is a not-resolved finding (rods called hollow with no cross-section or transmission view). The spine is a clean single-branch conversion argument, 16 nodes, four structure claims from one synthesis act converging on e14/e13; f6 and f7 are text-only OBS with no figs and correctly carry no mm_op. No invented panel ids.
